Scope: infrastructure over about 6.5 km² of the Fourth Industrial City in Riyadh: roads and tunnels, electrical, telecom, ICT and security networks, potable water and fire-fighting, irrigation, sewage and stormwater networks, and sewage and stormwater pumping stations.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 27.4% against 30.8% planned, the project is behind by 3.5% (SPI 0.89). It gained 2.1% this week against 0.7% planned, so the gap narrowed from 4.9% last week. Most of this week's gain came from procurement. Earthworks remain far ahead of plan, but procurement, the zone network works and the tunnels are still behind.

The schedule still finishes the project about eight months late. The P6 update uploaded this week (data date 02-Nov-2026) finishes the project on 25-Jan-2029, 240 days after the contract completion date of 30-May-2028 (last week: 01-Feb-2029, −247 days). The weekly report now gives the same date. In P6 the roads finish on 02-May-2027 and the MV network on 10-Nov-2027, against the contract milestone of 30-Sep-2026 for MV and road works.

Open issues and risks

IssueOwnerDetail
Clash with Green Riyadh servicesContractor / Green RiyadhAn air vent and cathodic protection on Road C8 clash with the works. Coordination with Green Riyadh's contractor is ongoing to get drawings and price the diversion. Rated critical; target moved to 15-Nov-2026.
Clash with ARAMCO gas linesContractor / ARAMCOWet and dry networks on Roads C8 and RD-L10 clash with two ARAMCO gas lines. Technical solutions were submitted and await ARAMCO's reply; solutions for telecom, sewage, MV, ICT and LV are already approved. Rated high; target moved to 30-Nov-2026.
Procurement delaysContractorPurchase orders had to be revised after the design changes, and material prices rose. Orders are issued and supply is under way. Rated high; the presentation targets 15-Nov-2026.
Progress behind planContractorProgress lags the schedule because of the master plan change (Wadi Al-Sulai) and the equipment shortage at the start. Equipment and network crews were increased; the presentation targets 30-Nov-2026. Rated critical.
SEC cable clashes (closed)Contractor / SECBoth clashes are now closed. On Road C2 the contractor appointed by SEC has started and is supporting the high-voltage cables. On Road C8 a start-of-work record was signed with SEC's contractor (Pillar).

Delay reasons stated in the report: the master layout changed after the Wadi Al-Sulai redesign, which changed the design of all networks; and equipment was short at the start of the project.

Data notes

This report uses the files uploaded for 02-Nov-2026 (weekly report, progress presentation, quantities and procurement file, P6 update) and, for this-week values, the 26-Oct-2026 report. Every progress percentage is physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. There is no S-curve section: the workbook's Physical-Chart Data sheet is empty.

  • The week number, 48, is the contract week stated on the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 48 of 130").
  • The workbook and the presentation also give a cost-based progress figure, labelled as actual progress in places. This report does not use it.
  • The forecast finish now agrees between the P6 update, the P6 extract and the General Information sheet (25-Jan-2029, −240 days). The Milestones sheet still shows no delay on any milestone.
  • Mobilisation finished on 29-Dec-2025 according to P6 and the presentation, but on 30-Mar-2026 according to the weekly report.
  • Earthworks man-hours did not change this week (74.0%), although the quantities show +10,000 m³ cut and +2,110 m³ fill.
  • The presentation's quantity slide repeats the 26-Oct-2026 quantities; this report uses the 02-Nov-2026 figures from the workbook and the quantities file.
  • Tunnel 01 concrete is 5,243 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet but 3,903 m³ on the Major sheet.
  • Quality: inspection requests show 490 issued but 1,687 closed and 236 pending, which cannot all be right. Cumulative inductions fell from 348 to 74 and the year-to-date man-hours equal the cumulative total, which suggests the HSE counters were reset.
  • Invoices: the workbook lists 8 invoices, 71,001,361 SAR gross, none approved by the MODON PM and none paid; the presentation shows 70,621,360 SAR invoiced and the same amount paid. The contract value of 445,000,000 SAR is called "including VAT" on the Conclusion sheet but "excluding VAT" in the bill breakdown.
  • The P6 update lists no total float for its activities, so milestone floats are not shown.
  • Several summary panels still show #REF! or #DIV/0! errors.
  • Photos: five are stamped 01–02 Nov 2026; the tunnel slab photo has no stamp. A prime-coat photo stamped 03-Nov-2026 (after the data date) was not used.
